title: Dry socket treatment after a tooth extraction
what: The doctor cleans the socket where the tooth was removed and puts in a medicated dressing. This eases the pain and helps the wound heal.
why: When 2 to 4 days after a tooth is removed, the pain gets worse instead of better, and there is a bad smell.
duration: the procedure usually takes 15 to 20 minutes; healing takes 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: When the tooth was removed and when the pain got worse
If you take blood thinners or hormones
If you are allergic to any medicines

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Do not smoke. It slows healing.

prepare.title: Rinsing
prepare.text: Do not rinse your mouth hard before the visit.

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: You can take a painkiller your doctor already allowed. Tell them what you took.

bring: Notes or instructions from the extraction, if you have them
steps: The doctor looks at the socket
If needed, you get numbing medicine
Food bits and the broken-down clot are removed
A medicated dressing or paste is placed
The doctor explains how to care for it at home
feel: After the dressing, the pain usually eases a lot within a day
after: Do not touch the socket with your tongue or fingers
Do not smoke or drink through a straw
The dressing is sometimes changed. Come back for your follow-up
Rinse and take medicines as the doctor said
red_flags: It is hard to swallow or open your mouth: see a doctor right away

faq.a: The blood clot in the socket broke down or washed out. It is more common in smokers and after a difficult extraction.
After treatment, it usually feels better within a day. It fully heals in 1 to 2 weeks.

reminders.text: Visit for your tooth socket soon. Do not smoke or rinse your mouth hard.
